chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:
He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who steals with stealthy embezzlement, he would not be cut, but he would be whipped with an intense whipping'.

key_terms.يُقْطَعْ: He is cut (referring to the hadd of amputation)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for theft by stealthy embezzlement in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi distinguishes khulsah (stealthy embezzlement or taking from a place of trust) from standard theft, ruling out the hadd of hand amputation in favor of severe flogging. This reflects the Shia juristic view that the strict conditions for hadd are not fully met in cases of embezzlement, allowing for ta'zir (discretionary punishment) to ensure justice. The ruling underscores the importance of context in applying divine penalties, balancing legal rigor with practical equity.
